title: Release caravan schedule and decomposition primer - May 2027 (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact working primer for the May 'caravan' release — a set of interdependent features and infra flips that will be rolled across regions over two weeks. The goal is to provide a small, mobile-friendly checklist and a decomposed schedule so ops can shepherd the launch without heavy ceremony.

Scope: (what's inside)
- Hosted API: route-weight rebalancing + streaming throughput fix (small model cache change)
- Dedicated: new autoscaler config + backpressure safe-mode toggle
- Console: rollout UI flag and rollout-telemetry toggle
- Runtime: kernel selector tweak (fallthrough to quantized path)

High-level caravan cadence (two-week window):
- Week A (canary cohort): 2027-05-10 -> 2027-05-14
  - Day 1 (Mon): small canary (2% traffic) in us-west1 only; monitor 30m, then 10x sampling for latency percentiles
  - Day 2 (Tue): expand to 5% if green; run long-tail latency smoke test (90m)
  - Day 3 (Wed): expand to 15% + begin dedicated autoscaler soak tests (2h)
  - Day 4 (Thu): regional canaries in eu-west1 (1%); check cross-region routing and KV cache warmup
  - Day 5 (Fri): pause for retro and adjustments; prepare staging-to-prod patch if needed
- Week B (gradual ramp): 2027-05-17 -> 2027-05-21
  - Day 6 (Mon): 30% traffic across wk1 regions; enable console rollout UI for internal beta orgs
  - Day 7-8 (Tue-Wed): 50% -> 75% expansions; dedicated capacity adjustments; monitor unit-cost metrics daily
  - Day 9 (Thu): global open (95%) with safety lanes; sampling set to 1/200 tokens for output quality checks
  - Day 10 (Fri): full ramp request (100%) only if all SLOs met for 48 hours

Milestones (must have signoffs):
- Preflight (48-72h before canary): infra smoke, synthetic QoE run, rollback playbook confirmed, SRE shift staffed
- Canary go (Day 1): Product/PM + SRE + Oncall Eng approval in #release-orchestra, recorded in handoff note
- Ramp gate (Day 6): cost and latency SLOs green for 48h and no quality regressions in eval harness

Minimal preflight checklist (compact):
- API keys and quotas verified for burst tests
- Canary config pushed to feature-flag service (flag id: FLAG-3172)
- Default KV cache warmup script committed (script: infra/warmup/kv-prefill.sh)
- Telemetry retention for traces set to 7d for this launch
- Smoke automation runbook mapped to playbook card: PB-705
- Pager escalation path sanity-checked (pager: eng-release-rotations)

Canary windows and scaling notes:
- Use staggered canary start times (00:00, 04:00, 08:00 UTC) to detect time-zone correlated issues
- Autoscaler safe-mode: start with conservative thresholds (cpu < 50%, queue < 500ms) and relax after day 3 if stable
- Burst capacity policy: allow up to 2x reserved for 10m bursts, with auto-throttle after 12m sustained

Signal thresholds (quick):
- Latency: p95 increase > 15% over baseline => HOLD expansion and page SRE
- Errors: 5xx rate > 0.8% sustained for 10m => ROLLBACK to previous model variant
- Quality regressions: eval delta > 2 BLEU/ROUGE points or customer-specified sample failures => pause and investigate
- Cost: unit-token cost > 1.6x forecast for 6h => reduce batch size or roll back quantization change

Fallback and compatibility map (short):
- If runtime kernel selector fails: fallback to kernel-v2 (fully validated) via emergency flag FLAG-3172-fallback
- If model variant introduces KV-miss storm: switch to read-through cache policy -> gh:platform#4760 rollback PR ready
- Cross-region routing: maintain routing weight shadow 0.1% to warm caches before expanding

Release notes (draft) - consumer-facing bullets:
- Performance: improved inference latency for common n-ctx lengths via smarter kernel selection (avg p50 -7%)
- Reliability: safer autoscaling defaults for Dedicated pools to reduce cold-starts during spikes
- Console: rollout UI exposes per-route rollout windows and telemetry toggle for admins
- Known issues: some very long-context prompts may see higher variance in p99 (investigating), temporary metrics gap in eu-west1 traces (agents: tracing-agent v1.9)

Developer/backstage notes for the release: (things ops will want in the ticket)
- PRs: platform/pull/4876, runtime/pull/221, console/pull/1310
- DB migration: none for this release (config-only)
- Feature flags: FLAG-3172 (primary), FLAG-3172-beta (internal), FLAG-3172-fallback (emergency)
- Quick rollout commands: 
  - apply canary: ./infra/releasectl apply --env=prod --flag=FLAG-3172 --pct=2 --region=us-west1
  - expand: ./infra/releasectl scale --pct=15 --monitor=latency --region=us-west1
  - emergency rollback: ./infra/releasectl rollback --tag=release-2027-05-caravan

Smoke tests (short list):
- smoke/latency-echo: 1k requests over 5m, check p95 and p99
- smoke/stream-integrity: simulate streaming with mid-stream token drop, ensure client reconnect metrics stable
- smoke/kv-warm: prefill 100k key prefixes then run percentile test

Post-release checklist (first 6h):
- Confirm telemetry ingestion healthy for traces and logs (SRE)
- Cost dashboard check and token unit economics (finops)
- Customer error sampling: run 200 live-sample evaluations, log any false-positive safety triggers (prod-capture)
- Nightly regression job scheduled to run drift checks against eval harness at 02:00 UTC

Rollback criteria (compact):
- Automatic rollback if 5xx > 1% sustained for 15m OR p95 > baseline+25% for 30m
- Manual rollback if combined customer-impact signals (support escalations + SRE pager) within 2h window

Owners & immediate action items (who does what):
- Priya R: release conductor and last-mile coordination (this doc maintainer)
- Ethan C: runtime lead — stand by for kernel selector telemetry and hotfix PRs
- Marta S: dedicated capacity & autoscaler tuning; prepare autoscaler-experiment dashboard
- Jonah P: console rollout UI and feature-flag gating; pushed flag rollouts and audit logs
- Oncall SRE (week): see rota board, but primary contact is listed in the ticket REL-2043

Open questions / risks to resolve before Day 1:
- Is the fallback kernel warm path tested under 50% traffic for long-tail cases? (Ethan)
- Do we need an escrow quota for third-party telemetry ingestion? (Finance/Infra)
- Should we compress sampling cadence for eval harness on Day 3 to catch quality regressions sooner? (Product)

Notes-to-self and quick heuristics:
- Keep expansion steps small in the first 72h. If any signal shows noise, revert to last stable rollout percentage and increase sample size rather than expand.
- Prefer quick, observable changes over multiple small config changes at once. One variable per day makes the forensics tractable.

Retrospective prompts (for post-mortem):
- What were the earliest signals that predicted trouble? Timing & channel?
- Did our fallbacks act as expected? If not, why?
- Cost impact: were adjustments to batch/cache the right lever?
- What docs or tooling felt missing during the first 24h?

Appendix: quick links and scripts
- Warmup script: infra/warmup/kv-prefill.sh
- Rollout helper: infra/releasectl README snippet (line ~120)
- Eval harness: evals/caravan-quick-check/README.md

---
Small and intentionally terse. Use this as the live working release index for the caravan. Update the canary timings and owners as we firm up the infra load tests this week.

End.
